entries.title: Jeremiah 32:1
segments: The tenth year of Zedekiah; within about a year of the final capture of the city.

vv 1-15. 
 
The purchase which Jeremiah made of Hanameel was a pledge from God to his covenant people, that though for a season excluded from the land of Canaan, they should yet be restored to the possession of it; so all the present partial and limited victories which God grants to his church over the kingdom of Satan, are earnests and pledges of the universal victory that is reserved for her in coming ages.

entries.title: Jeremiah 32:7
segments: The right of redemption is thine; the lands of the Israelites were inalienable; when a man had occasion to sell a field, his nearest kinsman had the right of purchasing it, and it returned to its former owner of his children at the year of jubilee.

entries.title: Jeremiah 32:11
segments: Sealed--open; two evidences of sale were prepared: the one sealed and carefully laid up for future use, in case of doubt or litigation; the other a copy not sealed and left open, that its contents might at any time be read.

entries.title: Jeremiah 32:15
segments: Shall be possessed again; that is, by the Jews in the way of regular sale and purchase, as was explained in
.  This implied the peaceable repossession of their own land, from which Nebuchadnezzar was about to carry them into captivity.

entries.title: Jeremiah 32:25
segments:
For the city is given; rather, "and yet the city is given."  The present condition of affairs seems to the prophet inconsistent with God's promise. 
 
We should not judge of the prospects of God's cause by present appearances, but by his promises.  The darkest nights of the church's affliction lead to a glorious dawn.

entries.title: Jeremiah 32:26
segments:
vv 26-44. 
 
God knows how to pour out his wrath upon his visible church for her sins in such a manner that her present overthrow shall be the means of her purification and renovation, and the introduction of a new and more glorious era in her history.

entries.title: Jeremiah 32:33
segments: Turned unto me the back, and not the face; gone away from me instead of coming to me.

entries.title: Jeremiah 32:36
segments: Ye say, It shall be delivered into the hand of the king of Babylon; the threatened delivery of Jerusalem into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar seemed to the people to be the extinction of all their hopes for the future.  God assures them that, though this shall take place, there shall be a future restoration.
